38	
39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
80	
81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88	
89	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
90	
91	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
92	
93	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
94	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
95	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
96	
97	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
98	  await page.goto('/products')
99	
100	  await instant(page, async () => {
101	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
102	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
103	    await link.click()
104	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
105	
106	    await expect(
107	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
108	    ).toBeVisible()
109	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
110	  })
111	})
112	```
113	
114	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
115	
116	### Static or cached content
117	
118	The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:

120	```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
121	// Before
122	<Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
123	// After
124	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
125	```

127	### Uncached content

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
270	
271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

578	title: instant
579	description: Configure instant navigation validation for a route segment.
580	related:
581	  title: Next Steps
582	  description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
583	  links:
584	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
585	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic
586	    - app/getting-started/caching
587	    - app/getting-started/revalidating
588	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
589	---
590	
591	The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.
592	
593	Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.
594	
595	When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.
596	
597	> **Good to know**:
598	>
599	> - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
600	> - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error.
601	> - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled.
602	
603	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
604	export const instant = true
605	
606	export default function Page() {
607	  return <div>...</div>
608	}
609	```
610	
611	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
612	export const instant = true
613	
614	export default function Page() {
615	  return <div>...</div>
616	}
617	```
618	
619	## Reference
620	
621	The export accepts:
622	
623	- **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay.
624	- **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)).
625	- An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level).
626	
627	### `level`
628	
629	Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment.
630	
631	```tsx filename="page.tsx"
632	export const instant = {
633	  level: 'warning',
634	}
635	```
636	
637	- **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected.
638	
639	In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`.
640	
641	When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults).
642	
643	### Disabling instant
644	
645	Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it.
646	
647	This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`.
648	
649	```tsx filename="app/tabs/layout.tsx"
650	export const instant = false
651	```
652	
653	```tsx filename="app/tabs/[tab]/page.tsx"
654	export const instant = true
655	```
656	
657	Navigations from outside into a tab are allowed to block at the layout. Navigations between tabs are validated for instant UI.
658	
659	You don't need to add `false` to ancestors of an instant page just because they do something blocking — a higher-up `instant = true` doesn't force its descendants to validate, and leaving an ancestor unconfigured is fine. Reach for `false` only when you've configured a deeper page as instant and need to exempt navigations that pass through a blocking ancestor.
660	
661	### Disabling static shell validation
662	
663	Cache Components also validates that each page in your app produces a non-empty static shell at prerender time. To opt a route out of this validation, ensure the highest `instant` config in the route's tree is `false` — a `false` higher in the tree takes precedence over any deeper `true` for the static-shell check.
664	
665	Setting `false` on the root layout disables static shell validation for the entire app. Place the `false` as low as possible — only as high as needed to cover the routes you want to opt out — so the rest of the app keeps validating.
666	
667	## How validation works
668	
669	`instant` triggers validation at every shared layout boundary in the route. Validation runs during development (on page loads and HMR updates) and surfaces errors in the dev error overlay.
670	
671	Each error identifies the component that would block navigation. The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `<Suspense>` boundary.
672	
673	## How `instant` differs from `ensureStatic`
674	
675	`instant` validates whether a navigation shows UI immediately. [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) requires selected server-rendered output to be static instead of rendered for each request. A route can be fully static and still block a navigation, for example when a Client Component loads data in the browser.
676	
677	## Configuring validation defaults
678	
679	By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`.
680	
681	```js filename="next.config.js"
682	module.exports = {
683	  experimental: {
684	    instantInsights: {
685	      validationLevel: 'warning',
686	    },
687	  },
688	}
689	```
690	
691	The supported levels are:
692	
693	- **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only).
694	- **`'manual-warning'`**: Only segments with an explicit `instant` are validated, at warning level (dev only).
695	
696	Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely.
697	
698	> **Good to know**:
699	>
700	> - The framework default may change in future versions to opt users into higher levels of validation. Because this feature is experimental, that change is not considered a breaking change. To pin a specific behavior, set `validationLevel` explicitly.
701	> - Framework-synthesized error routes (`/_global-error`, `/_not-found`) are excluded from implicit validation. To validate them, opt in explicitly with `instant`.
702	
703	## Inspecting loading states
704	
705	The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled:
706	
707	```js filename="next.config.js"
708	module.exports = {
709	  cacheComponents: true,
710	}
711	```
712	
713	Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then turn on **Pause on navigations**. While the toggle is on:
714	
715	- Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in.
716	- Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route.
717	
718	When the UI is frozen, click **Resume** to let the current navigation finish. The toggle stays on, so the next refresh or link click pauses too. Turn it off when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation.
719	
720	## Testing instant navigation
721	
722	The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. The testing API is available automatically in development. For a production build, enable [`experimental.exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild) in the test build. See the [guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for a full example.
723	
724	```typescript
725	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
726	```
727	
728	{/* TODO: remove when fixed and from prod-docs-release */}
729	
730	## Known issue: shared cookie across projects
731	
732	The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues.
733	
734	> **Good to know:** This will be fixed as part of stabilizing the feature.
735	
736	## TypeScript
737	
738	```tsx
739	type InstantConfig =
740	  | true
741	  | false
742	  | {
743	      level?: 'warning'
744	    }
745	
746	export const instant: InstantConfig = true
747	```
748	
749	## Version History
750	
751	| Version   | Changes                                                                            |
752	| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
753	| `v16.3.0` | `instant` export stabilized, replacing `unstable_instant` (Cache Components only). |

13	---
14	
15	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
16	
17	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
18	
19	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
20	
21	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
22	
23	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
24	
25	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
26	
27	Install the skill:
28	
29	```bash filename="Terminal"
30	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
31	```
32	
33	Then give the agent this prompt:
34	
35	```prompt
36	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
37	```
38	
39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.

81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
270	
271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

590	
591	The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.
592	
593	Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.
594	
595	When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.
596	
597	> **Good to know**:
598	>
599	> - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
600	> - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error.
601	> - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled.
602	
603	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
604	export const instant = true
605	
606	export default function Page() {
607	  return <div>...</div>
608	}
609	```
610	
611	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
612	export const instant = true
613	
614	export default function Page() {
615	  return <div>...</div>
616	}
617	```

619	## Reference
620	
621	The export accepts:
622	
623	- **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay.
624	- **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)).
625	- An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level).
626	
627	### `level`
628	
629	Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment.
630	
631	```tsx filename="page.tsx"
632	export const instant = {
633	  level: 'warning',
634	}
635	```
636	
637	- **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected.
638	
639	In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`.
640	
641	When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults).
642	
643	### Disabling instant
644	
645	Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it.
646	
647	This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. 648	
649	```tsx filename="app/tabs/layout.tsx"
650	export const instant = false
651	```
652	
653	```tsx filename="app/tabs/[tab]/page.tsx"
654	export const instant = true
655	```
656	
657	Navigations from outside into a tab are allowed to block at the layout. Navigations between tabs are validated for instant UI.
658	
659	You don't need to add `false` to ancestors of an instant page just because they do something blocking — a higher-up `instant = true` doesn't force its descendants to validate, and leaving an ancestor unconfigured is fine. 660	
661	### Disabling static shell validation
662	
663	Cache Components also validates that each page in your app produces a non-empty static shell at prerender time. 664	
665	Setting `false` on the root layout disables static shell validation for the entire app. Place the `false` as low as possible — only as high as needed to cover the routes you want to opt out — so the rest of the app keeps validating.
666	
667	## How validation works
668	
669	`instant` triggers validation at every shared layout boundary in the route. Validation runs during development (on page loads and HMR updates) and surfaces errors in the dev error overlay.
670	
671	Each error identifies the component that would block navigation. The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `<Suspense>` boundary.
672	
673	## How `instant` differs from `ensureStatic`
674	
675	`instant` validates whether a navigation shows UI immediately. 676	
677	## Configuring validation defaults
678	
679	By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`.
680	
681	```js filename="next.config.js"

683	  experimental: {
684	    instantInsights: {

686	    },
687	  },
688	}
689	```
690	
691	The supported levels are:
692	
693	- **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only).

695	
696	Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely.

703	## Inspecting loading states
704	
705	The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled:
706	
707	```js filename="next.config.js"
708	module.exports = {
709	  cacheComponents: true,
710	}
711	```
712	
713	Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then turn on **Pause on navigations**. While the toggle is on:
714	
715	- Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in.
716	- Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route.
717	
718	When the UI is frozen, click **Resume** to let the current navigation finish. The toggle stays on, so the next refresh or link click pauses too. Turn it off when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation.
719	
720	## Testing instant navigation
721	
722	The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. 726	```

731

The project title now loads with the prefetch from the dashboard, so it shows instantly when you click through. The description and activity list aren't fetched until you actually navigate.

**What changed:**

1. **`next.config.ts`**: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. Without it, `prefetch={true}` downloads the whole destination page, and the `navigation()` call below has no effect on that link.
2. **`app/page.tsx`**: the dashboard's project links now use `prefetch={true}`. That's needed because the title depends on `slug`. By default a link only prefetches the parts of a page that are the same for every URL, and those can't include anything that depends on the slug.
3. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**: split the page into two `<Suspense>` boundaries:
   - `ProjectTitle` reads `params` and calls the cached `getProjectTitle`, so the prefetch can fill it in ahead of the click.
   - `ProjectDetails` calls `await navigation()` (from `next/cache`) before reading `params` and calling `getProjectDetails`. That keeps the slow (800ms) details out of the prefetch: they render only when you navigate, with "Loading details..." showing until then. `getProjectDetails` keeps its `'use cache'`.

Before, the title and details were fetched together with `Promise.all`, so the title couldn't appear until the slow details had loaded too.
